g4ela-22-1-morphology: New roots this week. One means push. One means hold. Think of a printing press pushing ink onto paper, or a jar that holds jam. Every word in the quilt is pushing something or holding something. Ask which one, then sew.
g4ela-22-2-spelling: These endings turn a word into a describing word. Here’s the tricky part. Some starting words end in a silent e, and that e drops off before the ending. Some lose nothing at all. So don’t trust your ears. Look hard at the starting word, then build.
g4ela-22-3-grammar: Here’s a writer’s trick. When a sentence needs two little helper words to show how someone moved, the verb underneath is usually too weak. Swap in one strong verb, and the helpers can go. Say both versions out loud. Which one sounds like someone sneaking past a guard?
g4ela-22-4-grammar: Last day with adverbs, and today you’re the editor. Some little words sound like they add a lot, but say nothing at all. Read each sentence without the extra word. If nothing is lost, cut it. If the verb feels weak, find a stronger one.
